kilauea_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY DAILY UPDATE
kilauea_notices.message: HVO Kilauea YELLOW/ADVISORY - The Halema'uma'u eruption of Kīlauea remains paused following episode 55 on October 17. The forecast for episode 56 fountaining is Nov. 3-7, 2026.
kilauea_notices.detail: Overview: The summit eruption of Kīlauea in Halemaʻumaʻu remains paused, although there was a small overflow and several spatter events associated with gas pistoning prior to midnight. Slow, steady inflation continues at the summit. Based on current slow inflation trends and assuming magma chamber inflation continues to follow similar patterns to those established during episodes prior to 54, the forecast window for episode 56 fountaining is November 3-7, 2026. Summit Observations: Strong glow was seen from both vents last night. An active lava surface could be seen rising and falling several times in the north vent accompanied by vigorous spattering associated with gas pistoning overnight. One very small overflow began at 8:31 p.m. HST and lasted approximately eight minutes prior to drainback. Less frequent spatter and occasional flames were seen from the combined southwest vent overnight. Poor weather obscured the webcams for several times throughout the night and early morning. Seismic tremor continued yesterday and overnight, marked by alternating continuous tremor and periods of stronger pulses or bursts every few hours. The tremor pulses are typically associated with increased glow and gas emissions with dimming glow associated with periods of lower tremor in between the pulses characteristic of gas pistoning withing the vents.. There were 11 earthquakes less than M1.5 recorded at the summit in the past 24 hours, all of which occurred in the southern part of Kaluapele (Kīlauea caldera). Summit tiltmeters have recorded an overall positive trend since the end of episode 55, with several small, short-term oscillations. The general pattern remains consistent with post-fountaining re-inflation observed during previous inter-episode pauses. The Uēkahuna tiltmeter (UWD) has recorded an increase of approximately 1.2 microradians in the past 24 hours for a total of 17.2 microradians of tilt recovered since the end of episode 55. Sulfur dioxide (SO2) emission rates during inter-episode pauses typically range from 1,000 to 5,000 tonnes per day. This morning, volcanic gases can be seen lofting straight upward from the vents in the light winds. Rift Zone Observations: Rates of seismicity and ground deformation remain low in the East Rift Zone and Southwest Rift Zone. SO2 emissions from the East Rift Zone remain below the detection limit. Analysis: Following episode 55 on October 17, 2026, summit tiltmeters initially recorded a typical post-fountaining recovery, with a steady upward trend that gradually slowed and was interrupted by several small fluctuations. Tilt has continued to increase slowly following a brief negative trend on October 26. While the there have been minor fluctuations in tilt over the past week, the overall tilt pattern is a slow, steady increase. The fluctuations in tilt rate result in adjustments to the modeled forecast window for episode 56 fountaining, which is now November 3–7, 2026. Given the unusual buildup to episode 55, uncertainty remains as to whether summit deformation will continue to follow a sufficiently consistent pattern to allow for precise forecasting of the next episode. Kīlauea has been erupting episodically since December 23, 2024, from two primary vents (north and south) within Halemaʻumaʻu at the summit. Lava fountaining episodes generally last less than 12 hours and are separated by pauses of two or more weeks. The buildup to episode 55 differed substantially from previous episodes, with summit tiltmeters recording positive tilt beyond levels typically observed before fountaining, suggesting continued pressurization of the summit magma chamber. This prolonged buildup was punctuated by extended periods of negative or relatively stable tilt, rather than the more consistent upward trends observed before earlier episodes. mauna_loa_notices.title: HAWAIIAN VOLCANO OBSERVATORY MONTHLY UPDATE
mauna_loa_notices.message: HVO Mauna Loa GREEN/NORMAL - Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues.
mauna_loa_notices.detail: Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks. No earthquakes occurred directly beneath Mokuʻāweoweo. Data from Global Positioning System (GPS) instruments on Mauna Loa showed slight inflation across the summit region in the past month. Oscillations between contraction and inflation patterns during non-eruptive periods are normal, but inflation has been the dominant trend since the 2022 eruption, consistent with magma refilling the summit reservoir system. Gas and temperature data from a station on Mauna Loa's Southwest Rift Zone indicate these values are at background levels, with little change relative to previous months. HVO continues to closely monitor Mauna Loa and will issue another update in one month, or earlier, should conditions change significantly.
